issues.legal_issue: The bar on claims concerning irregularities in publishing or conducting a revenue sale does not bar a challenge to the confirmation authority’s failure to perform its separate statutory duty at confirmation.
material_facts: The appellant did not apply within 30 days of the sale to set it aside.
After confirmation, the appellant challenged whether the confirmation authority had considered the purchaser’s existing landholding and the effect of the purchase on the statutory landholding limit.
The challenge concerned the authority’s consideration at confirmation, not an irregularity or mistake in publishing or conducting the sale.
issues.conclusion: The objection to the confirmation authority’s failure to consider the landholding restriction was not barred by the rule barring untimely claims about irregularities or mistakes in publishing or conducting the sale, and the confirmed order could be challenged in writ proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 285-K bars claims based on irregularity or mistake in publishing or conducting a sale when no timely application is made under Rule 285-I, subject to its fraud-suit proviso. Rule 285-J separately requires the Collector, at confirmation, to satisfy himself that the purchase would not contravene Section 154. A challenge to failure to perform that confirmation-stage duty is not a claim about irregularity or mistake in publishing or conducting the sale. The Court treated writ proceedings as a means to challenge the confirmation order for failure to consider a legally relevant factor.

predicates.challenge_to_confirmed_revenue_sale: The affected owner challenged an order confirming a revenue sale.
predicates.no_timely_sale_set_aside_application: The affected owner did not apply within the allowed period to set aside the sale.
predicates.challenge_concerns_confirmation_review: The challenge concerned whether the authority considered a matter it was required to assess when confirming the sale, rather than an irregularity in publishing or conducting it.
predicates.confirmation_duty_challenge_not_barred: A challenge to the confirmation authority’s failure to perform its confirmation-stage duty is not barred as an untimely sale-irregularity claim.

issues.definition: When an affected owner challenges a confirmed revenue sale without a timely sale-setting-aside application, a challenge about the authority’s confirmation-stage review is not barred.

issues.legal_issue: A claim based on notice or other irregularity in publishing or conducting a revenue sale is barred if the affected owner had notice and did not apply to set the sale aside within the prescribed period.
material_facts: The Commissioner and the High Court found that notices of the sale proceedings had been given to the appellant and that she refused the notice for the sale date.
The appellant did not apply within 30 days of the sale to set it aside on grounds of irregularity or mistake.
The appellant later sought to raise the absence of notice and other matters concerning the sale proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The appellant could not raise the absence-of-notice claim or other claims of irregularity or mistake in publishing or conducting the sale after failing to apply within 30 days; those claims were foreclosed.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 285-H and 285-I provide for applications to set aside a sale, including an application based on material irregularity or mistake in publishing or conducting it. Rule 285-K bars claims on those grounds when no timely Rule 285-I application is made, subject to the proviso permitting a civil suit on the ground of fraud. The Court relied on the findings that the appellant had notice and refused the sale notice.

rule.if: challenge_to_revenue_sale and actual_notice_of_sale and no_timely_sale_irregularity_application and challenge_concerns_sale_notice_or_conduct

predicates.challenge_to_revenue_sale: An affected owner challenged a revenue sale.
predicates.actual_notice_of_sale: The affected owner received notice of the sale proceedings or refused the sale notice.
predicates.no_timely_sale_irregularity_application: The affected owner did not apply within the allowed period to set aside the sale for irregularity or mistake.
predicates.challenge_concerns_sale_notice_or_conduc: The challenge concerns notice, publication, or conduct of the sale.
predicates.untimely_sale_irregularity_claim_barred: A claim about notice or other sale irregularity is barred when it is not raised through a timely application.

issues.definition: When an affected owner had notice of a revenue sale, failed to apply promptly to set it aside, and later challenges notice or sale conduct, the untimely sale-irregularity claim is barred.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory restriction on a purchaser’s aggregate landholding applies to revenue execution sales, and confirmation requires an actual, evidence-based assessment rather than reliance on the purchaser’s affidavit alone.
material_facts: The sale transferred 8.50 acres to the purchaser, and the appellant alleged that the purchaser already held about five acres.
The purchaser disputed that allegation and supplied an affidavit stating that her holding after the purchase would not exceed the statutory limit.
The confirmation order merely recorded that the affidavit was attached and did not show examination of relevant revenue records or other evidence.
The Commissioner did not resolve the competing claims about the purchaser’s holding, and the High Court proceeded on the view that the restriction did not apply to execution sales.
issues.conclusion: The landholding restriction applied to the revenue sale. Merely attaching the purchaser’s affidavit did not establish the confirmation authority’s required satisfaction; the authority had to apply its mind to relevant evidence, including the relevant revenue records.
issues.legal_principle: Section 154(1) restricts a transfer that would cause the transferee’s aggregate holding, together with the relevant family holding, to exceed the prescribed limit. Rule 285-J expressly requires the Collector at confirmation to be satisfied that the purchase will not contravene Section 154, so the restriction applies to revenue sales as well as voluntary transfers. The Court held that satisfaction requires evidence of the authority’s application of mind; a purchaser’s affidavit merely attached to the order is insufficient. It rejected the contrary view in Gaon Sabha v. Deputy Director of Consolidation, Lucknow, insofar as that view excluded revenue sales from the restriction. Kripa Shankar v. Director of Consolidation concerned an earlier gift and the then-existing Section 163, and did not determine whether this revenue sale should be confirmed; Section 163 had been deleted and Section 166 introduced with effect from 3 June 1981. The Court did not need to decide whether this sale was void under Section 166.

rule.if: revenue_execution_sale and purchaser_acquires_land and purchaser_holding_may_exceed_limit and confirmation_relies_only_on_purchaser_affidavit

predicates.revenue_execution_sale: The property was transferred through a revenue sale carried out to enforce recovery.
predicates.purchaser_acquires_land: A purchaser acquired land through the sale.
predicates.purchaser_holding_may_exceed_limit: There was a factual basis to question whether the purchaser’s aggregate holding after acquisition would exceed the applicable limit.
predicates.confirmation_relies_only_on_purchaser_af: The confirmation authority relied only on the purchaser’s affidavit and did not demonstrate consideration of relevant records or other evidence.
predicates.confirmation_requires_evidence_based_rev: The authority must assess relevant evidence and apply its mind to whether the acquisition complies with the landholding restriction.

issues.definition: When a revenue-sale purchaser may exceed the landholding limit and confirmation rests only on the purchaser’s affidavit, confirmation requires an evidence-based review of the purchaser’s holding.

issues.legal_issue: Where a confirmed sale is vitiated by failure to consider the landholding restriction, the Court may decline to remand and grant final relief based on the circumstances of the proceedings.
material_facts: The confirmation order did not show that the authority had properly considered the purchaser’s landholding.
The appellant had remained in possession during the proceedings and had obtained an order maintaining the status quo.
The proceedings had continued for a substantial period, and the appellant deposited money in Court after being directed to do so.

The Commissioner had earlier given the appellant an opportunity to pay the debt, and the Court considered that the recovery amount and interest could be paid from the deposited funds, with any deficiency made good by the appellant.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the confirmation order, the Commissioner’s order, and the High Court judgment; it declined to remand the matter, directed that the sale not be confirmed, and allowed the appellant to retain the property subject to payment of the recoverable amount and interest. The purchaser was to receive back her deposit with interest.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its authority to grant final relief rather than remit a matter where, in light of the long-running proceedings, the appellant’s continued possession, the deposit made in Court, and the opportunity to satisfy the debt, remand was not appropriate. The Court did not decide whether the sale was void under Section 166, finding it unnecessary to do so to dispose of the appeal.

rule.if: appeal_against_confirmed_revenue_sale and confirmation_order_vitiated and prolonged_proceedings and appellant_remained_in_possession and appellant_deposited_recovery_funds

predicates.appeal_against_confirmed_revenue_sale: The proceeding was an appeal challenging an order confirming a revenue sale.
predicates.confirmation_order_vitiated: The confirmation order was invalid because the authority failed to consider a matter it was required to assess.
predicates.prolonged_proceedings: The dispute had continued for a substantial period before final decision.
predicates.appellant_remained_in_possession: The affected owner remained in possession of the property during the proceedings.
predicates.appellant_deposited_recovery_funds: The affected owner deposited funds in Court that could be applied toward the recovery debt and related interest.
predicates.sale_not_confirmed_and_appellant_retains: The sale is not confirmed and the affected owner retains the property subject to satisfying the recoverable debt and interest.

issues.definition: When a confirmed revenue sale is invalid, the proceedings are prolonged, the affected owner has remained in possession and has deposited recovery funds, the Court may decline remand, refuse confirmation, and allow retention subject to payment.
